chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated to us, from Ibn Sinan, from Hafss, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

There is no believing servant who commits a sin but that Allah delays [its recording] for him for seven hours of the day. If he repents, nothing is recorded against him; and if he does not, one evil deed is recorded against him. So 'Abbād al-Baṣrī came to him and said to him: We have been informed that you said: 'There is no servant who commits a sin but that Allah delays [its recording] for him for seven hours of the day.' He said: 'That is not how I said it, but I said: There is no believing servant who commits a sin but that Allah delays [its recording] for him for seven hours of his day. That is how I said it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the specific condition for Allah delaying the recording of a sin for seven hours?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the divine delay of seven hours for recording a sin applies specifically to a 'believing servant' (abd mu'min), not just any servant. If the believer repents within this period, the sin is forgiven; otherwise, it is recorded as a single evil deed. This distinction highlights the elevated spiritual status of the *abd mu'min*, whose minor sins are temporarily suspended to allow for immediate repentance, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interplay between divine mercy and human agency in the process of *tawbah*.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 1.Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, “Al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd narrated to us, from Ibn Sinān, from Ḥafṣ who said, ‘I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (a) say, “There is no believing servant who commits a sin but that Allah delays for him [the recording of that sin] for seven hours of the day. If he repents [in that time], nothing is recorded against him but if he fails to do so, one evil deed is recorded against him.” So ʿAbbād al-Baṣrī came to him and said, “We have been informed that you said there is no servant who commits a sin but that Allah delays [its recording] for him for seven hours of the day?” So he (a) replied, “That is not how I said it. Rather, I said: there is no believing servant who commits a sin but that Allah delays [its recording] for him for seven hours of his day – that is how I said it.”’”[1]
